text:
[LREG.8.1] **The regex syntax is RE2.** A pattern means what RE2's
published specification says it means. DS defines no dialect of its
own, admits no superset, and the choice is a commitment of the
language rather than of any particular runtime.

Linear-time evaluation in the input length, and the absence of
catastrophic backtracking, **follow from** RE2. They are consequences
of the choice, not an alternative way of satisfying it: an engine
exhibiting those properties under a *different* syntax — POSIX ERE,
for instance — is **not** conforming, because the patterns an author
may write would differ. Equally, an engine offering RE2's syntax plus
backtracking extensions (PCRE-family) is not conforming, because the
linear-time guarantee would no longer hold.
